products.name: Content Analytics
products.title: Adobe Content Analytics
products.what: Content Analytics helps marketers to understand how content impacts the key performance indicators that a business has defined.

source.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview

products.notes: Adobe licenses Content Analytics as a product of its own, but it is set up and read inside Experience Platform and Customer Journey Analytics, so the work happens in the Customer Journey Analytics interface (Data Management, Content Analytics Configuration) whether or not your client owns Customer Journey Analytics. It needs Experience Platform Web SDK, Mobile SDK or source connectors for data. Each sandbox allows one configuration and one connection. Featurization supports English only, Content Analytics is not a HIPAA-Ready service, and Privacy and Security Shield labels and customer managed keys do not cover its experiences and assets. CA04 covers Google Ads and Meta Ads, and the paid media channel is not offered on Experience Platform deployments on AWS; the other ad networks are in left_out. Adobe's own guide says to plan 4 to 6 hours for the first setup of the standalone product, plus testing. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: A Content Analytics license: Adobe sells it as a standalone product and sets it up inside Experience Platform and Customer Journey Analytics
Data collected with the Experience Platform Edge Network (Web SDK, Mobile SDK or Server API) or through Experience Platform source connectors
The featurization service's User Agent and IP address allow-listed on your client's site, so the service can read the pages and images
A Customer Journey Analytics Product Administrator role with permission to manage connections and data views, plus Experience Platform and Data Collection permissions
One Content Analytics configuration for each sandbox
For page (experience) reporting: pages whose text can be reproduced from the page URL and does not depend on cookies or personalization
English content: the featurization service supports English only
Not for regulated health data: Content Analytics is not a HIPAA-Ready service
Access is given by data view: there is no Content Analytics permission of its own

prereq_sources.quote: Content Analytics is licensed as a standalone product, but the configuration happens within Experience Platform and Customer Journey Analytics.
These content experience events require the data to be collected with the Experience Platform Edge Network (Web SDK, Mobile SDK, Server API) or through Experience Platform source connectors.
You have allow-listed the User Agent and IP address for the featurization service that is used in Content Analytics.
You have a Customer Journey Analytics Product Administrator role, with the additional permissions to manage connections and to manage data views.
You can only have one Content Analytics configuration per sandbox in your organization.
The text content seen by any given user can be reproduced using the page URL and does not depend on cookies or other personalization mechanisms.
Content Analytics supports featurization in English only.
Also, Content Analytics is not a HIPAA-Ready service.
There is no Content Analytics permission that you can configure to enable or disable Content Analytics access for individual users or groups of users.

tiers.name: Adobe Content Analytics (standalone license)
tiers.what: The product Adobe sells today, licensed per million Content Rows of Data. Clients without a Customer Journey Analytics license also get Analytics Behavioral Rows of Data. All six lines assume it.
tiers.quote: Analytics Behavioral Rows of Data are Core Data and are only available to Customers that have licensed Adobe Content Analytics without an accompanying Customer Journey Analytics (Foundation, Select, Prime, or Ultimate) license.

tiers.name: Content Analytics as a Customer Journey Analytics add-on (no longer sold)
tiers.what: Adobe no longer licenses Content Analytics as an add-on to Customer Journey Analytics, and an existing add-on cannot be renewed. A client that has the add-on moves to the standalone product at renewal.
tiers.quote: Customers who wish to license Adobe Content Analytics must purchase the standalone version of Adobe Content Analytics.

tiers.name: Limits in the standalone license
tiers.what: One connection for each sandbox, 15 data views for each connection and five sandboxes, which caps how many brands or sites one license can report on separately.
tiers.quote: Connections 1 connection per Sandbox ... Data Views 15 per connection

tiers.name: Paid media channel
tiers.what: Needs Experience Platform source connectors to the ad networks and is not offered on Customer Journey Analytics and Experience Platform deployments on AWS. CA04 needs it.
tiers.quote: The paid media channel is not available for Customer Journey Analytics and Experience Platform deployments on AWS.

products.notes: It has a paid license of its own and needs an active Adobe Target or Journey Optimizer license; Adobe's product description says it is not compatible with Journey Optimizer Prime Starter or Ultimate Starter. products.name: Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
products.title: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
products.what: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition lets marketing and sales teams orchestrate account-based experiences and qualify buying groups for specific products across the entire customer lifecycle.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Documentation

products.notes: Built on Experience Platform with Real-Time CDP B2B: Experience Platform is the data store for accounts, people and opportunities, and the B2B Edition owns the account journeys, buying groups and buying group roles. Each subscription comes with a dedicated Marketo Engage instance that supplies entitlements and backend services such as email delivery, sender configuration and branding domains; it is separate from your client's production Marketo Engage instance and does not store the journeys. Audience membership is evaluated once a day, so qualifying accounts enter a published journey within 24 hours. These lines cover account journeys with email; the parts of the product the lines leave out are in left_out. Marketo Engage journey actions, the Real-Time CDP data path and Target audiences are costed on the connections ajob2b-marketo, ajob2b-rtcdp and ajob2b-target. Adobe Marketo Optimizer is a different product with its own guide. Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none.
prereqs: A Journey Optimizer B2B Edition license, sized by Engageable Businessperson Profiles
Real-Time CDP B2B Edition (or B2P Edition): the B2B schemas only qualify for Real-Time Customer Profile with it
The dedicated Marketo Engage instance that comes with each subscription, set up for email tracking and deliverability
DNS access for the tracking CNAME, branding domains, DKIM, SPF, DMARC and MX records
An Experience Platform API credential and Postman, to run Adobe's namespace and schema utility
An Account Name on every account record: accounts without one are left out of account journeys
Daily timing accepted: audience membership is evaluated once a day
Limits to plan for, such as 100 account journeys active at one time

notes: Content Analytics has no documented connection to the other products of the Omnichannel play (AEM Sites, AEM Assets, Journey Optimizer, Experimentation Accelerator), rechecked Nov 10 2026. Its documented ties are Customer Journey Analytics, Real-Time CDP, Marketing Campaign Analytics and GenStudio for Performance Marketing (in portal_acquisition_insights.json) and, new in this file, Coworker (ca-cw).

Content Analytics also appears in the Customer Acquisition and Content Reporting and Insights plays; its other connections are in portal_acquisition_insights.json and are rechecked in that file, not here.

Content Analytics licensing: Experience League now says it is licensed as a standalone product with the configuration inside Experience Platform and Customer Journey Analytics, and Adobe's Customer Journey Analytics product description says the add-on to Customer Journey Analytics is no longer sold. The product's tiers carry both. No needs id was added.

Experimentation Accelerator has a paid license of its own and needs an active Adobe Target or Journey Optimizer license (not a Journey Optimizer Starter package). Target is now a connection of its own (xa-target). Adobe's old business.adobe.com accelerator page could not be read from this environment.

commerce-aemsites: Adobe says the CIF storefront and CIF Core Components are in maintenance mode and should not be used in new projects, and recommends Edge Delivery with the Adobe Commerce Storefront (the eds product, connection commerce-eds). The CIF add-on is still the documented way to bring product data into AEM authoring for headless builds. It is an extra module provisioned by Adobe through the sales rep.
commerce-aemsites has one data flow (Commerce to AEM). The CIF pages describe AEM calling the Commerce GraphQL endpoint but do not describe data written back to Commerce.

commerce-aemassets requires licenses for Adobe Commerce, AEM Assets and AEM Dynamic Media; Commerce on Cloud (PaaS) needs 2.4.5 or later; Commerce and AEM Assets must be in the same IMS organization; configuration works at the global scope only. Adobe states the integration itself has no additional cost. Custom matching needs App Builder.

aemsites-aemassets: when Sites and Assets run in the same AEM environment they share one repository and no connection setup is needed; XC01 applies when the DAM is a separate environment. Dynamic Media with OpenAPI needs AEM Assets as a Cloud Service and AEM Dynamic Media licenses.

aemassets-ajo: Journey Optimizer is replacing its Asset Selector and Content Fragment selector with AEM Content Advisor; existing integrations keep working during the transition. The Dynamic Media part is only for Dynamic Media as a Cloud Service customers.
aemsites-ajo: for healthcare customers the Content Fragment integration needs the Journey Optimizer Healthcare Shield and AEM Extended Security for Healthcare add-ons.

ajob2b-aemassets needs AEM Assets as a Cloud Service and Dynamic Media licenses with Dynamic Media with OpenAPI enabled, works only with Delivery tier repositories, supports images only, allows one DAM source at a time when authoring, and its certificates expire every 365 days. Adobe's product description says the B2B Edition can connect to one Experience Manager repository, while the guide describes adding more than one; confirm with Adobe before planning several.

commerce-ajob2b possible route, not documented: Commerce Data Connection sends storefront and B2B requisition list events to Experience Platform, and the B2B Edition can listen to profile-enabled Experience Platform events ingested by streaming. That needs Experience Platform (Real-Time CDP) and no Adobe page describes it end to end. Rechecked Nov 10 2026: the B2B Edition guide still names Commerce only as event names in the engagement score weighting list.

Hours are our estimates for a mid-market client; Adobe publishes none. Monthly lines (SI06, AS06, CA06, EX06, JB06) are inferred from Adobe's ongoing tasks (post go-live monitoring, asset reports, insight reviews, experiment KPIs, dashboards); Adobe publishes no monthly service list.

Quotes were script-checked against downloaded copies of every cited page (whitespace and curly quotes normalized). business.adobe.com pages could not be downloaded from this environment and were read with a web fetch only; none is cited as a line source.

Nov 10 2026 recheck: every line evidence, prerequisite, tier, availability, not-documented and left-out quote on the in-scope entries (ca, xa, ajob2b, ajo-xa, ajob2b-aemassets and the five new connections) was script-checked against a fresh download of its page (tags stripped, whitespace and curly quotes normalized, lower-cased, exact substring). The Oct 30 entries for AEM Sites, AEM Assets and their connections are copied through unchanged and were not rechecked here. business.adobe.com and www.adobe.com pages were not read.

Journey Optimizer B2B Edition and Marketo Engage (Nov 10 2026): Adobe's overview says the two run on separate systems, each with its own data store. A dedicated Marketo Engage instance comes with every B2B Edition subscription for entitlements and backend services such as email delivery, and a client's existing Marketo Engage instances can be connected for journey actions (ajob2b-marketo). Marketo data reaches journeys through Experience Platform (marketo-rtcdp).

Adobe Marketo Optimizer is a separate product with its own guide and product description. It is paired with one Marketo Engage instance, syncs leads and companies with it directly, and does not require Real-Time CDP. It is not in the catalog. Neither guide says one product replaces the other.

Journey Optimizer B2B Edition needs Real-Time CDP B2B Edition or B2P Edition for account audiences and for its B2B schemas to qualify for Real-Time Customer Profile (ajob2b-rtcdp). The catalog's rtcdp product is Real-Time CDP in general; the edition is carried as a prerequisite and a tier.

ajob2b-target was not one of the pairs named for this recheck; it is written up because the B2B Edition guide documents it with setup steps. It runs through the Adobe Target destination in Real-Time CDP.

Experimentation Accelerator and Customer Journey Analytics: the accelerator imports a primary metric from Customer Journey Analytics or Adobe Analytics when one of them is the experiment's reporting source. That stays the product line EX04 with an ext; it could become an xa-cja connection if Adam wants the line drawn on the canvas.
New service ids in this file: XH01 to XH11. No id repeats one in sow/canvas/catalog.json or in any sow/canvas/research/*.json (checked by script Nov 10 2026).
